headline: Cryosite CEO outlines 3-5 year ambition to expand beyond Australia into Asia-Pacific and globally, targeting vertical integration in biological materials logistics.
reasoning: Andrew Kerr, CEO of Cryosite, describes plans to accelerate expansion into a new facility and grow beyond Australia into the Asia-Pacific region and potentially globally within 3-5 years. The company operates in the ultra-cold storage and logistics niche (-80°C and -196°C), serving large pharmaceutical companies conducting R&D and clinical trials for biotech breakthroughs. Kerr notes the Australian market remains fragmented in clinical trials and biological materials, but expects vertical integration between depot sites and logistics providers to emerge, similar to trends already seen in the US and Europe. He sees Cryosite well positioned to capitalise on this consolidation.
quote: I don't see CRI site as being an Australian business in 3 to 5 years. There are huge opportunities for us to scale and grow, not only domestically, but I think within the Asia-Pacific region. And, you know, hopefully globally. Australia is still a fairly fragmented market in terms of clinical trials and biological materials. Whereas, you know, we've seen certainly in the US and Europe, this vertical integration occurring between depot sites like ourselves and logistics providers or transport providers that ultimately, you know, operate that last mile service to the clinical trial site, the hospital or the university. So I think we'll see some similar themes come through in the Australian market in the next, you know, I'd say near future. And, um, you know, we're certainly positioned to capitalise on that.
episode_title: How Cryosite is turning frozen assets into hot growth

headline: Cryosite posts 20% NPAT growth driven by capacity expansion into ultra-cold and cryogenic storage segment
reasoning: Cryosite reported a trading update for FY26 showing net profit after tax up 20% and revenue up 18%, with margins expanding. Growth is capacity and utilisation-led, driven by rising demand for ultra-frozen and cryogenic storage from big pharma and biotech clients conducting multi-year clinical trials. The company recently acquired a second warehouse facility in western Sydney, doubling capacity overnight, which will be built out on a demand-led basis. Management believes the cell and gene therapy segment — a key driver of cryogenic demand — will grow at approximately 30% per annum for the next ten years, and Cryosite is one of the only operators in Australia capable of handling clinical trial materials at -80°C and -196°C. The company is strongly cash flow generative and does not anticipate needing to raise external capital to fund the expansion.
quote: Well, I think what's most encouraging about this is this this is really a capacity and utilization led growth story. Um, you know, we we ran into a bit of a problem this year where, you know, it was a good problem to have. We started to run out of capacity at our existing, uh, headquarters, which is in Ferndale Street in western Sydney. Um, so the board made a, you know, quite a bold but conscious decision to expand capacity. We acquired a second warehouse facility, which is about 15 minutes drive from our headquarters. Um, that second facility has doubled our capacity overnight. Um, you know, these these clients, we're dealing with big pharma, even small biotechs. Um, the the research and development they do into these products can last three, five, ten years in some cases. So they really need visibility on, you know, where this product is going to be stored and need to have assurances around your ability to, to keep receiving and handling these products.
episode_title: How Cryosite is turning frozen assets into hot growth

headline: Cryosite CEO identifies Cryoport (Nasdaq: CYRX) as the closest listed peer, active in cell and gene therapy cold-chain logistics.
reasoning: Andrew Kerr identifies Cryoport, listed on the Nasdaq, as the only comparable listed peer to Cryosite. Cryoport is active in -80°C and -196°C storage and logistics for cell and gene therapy, Car-T therapy, and stem cell therapy — the same segments Cryosite is targeting. The reference is used to contextualise Cryosite's market positioning and growth potential rather than as a direct investment recommendation on Cryoport itself.
quote: I think that really the only listed peer that's comparable to us would be Cryo port, which is listed on the Nasdaq in the US. They are very active in the -80 and -196 cell and gene therapy, Car-T therapy, stem cell therapy, all the things that we're seeing here.

sector: Cell & Gene Therapy / Cryogenic Biologics Logistics
headline: Cell and gene therapy sector expected to grow ~30% per annum for the next decade, creating strong structural tailwind for cryogenic storage infrastructure
reasoning: Andrew Kerr highlighted that the cell and gene therapy market is expected to grow at approximately 30% per annum for the next ten years, citing general market consensus. This accelerating growth is creating significant demand for ultra-cold storage and logistics infrastructure capable of handling materials at -80°C and -196°C. Advanced therapies including mRNA vaccines, Car-T therapies, and cell and gene therapies all require specialist cryogenic handling, and there are very few operators globally capable of meeting these requirements at clinical trial scale.
quote: I'll go back to the ultra frozen and cryogenic segment that I talked about before, because really, that is where we're seeing huge, huge macroeconomic sort of factors coming into play there. There's accelerating growth year on year. I think the general consensus really amongst the market is that the, you know, selling gene therapies in particular, will probably grow at about 30% per annum for the next ten years. And we're certainly seeing that level of demand come through in our business. As I said, we're we're really one of the only operators in the market that can handle clinical trials at those temperature ranges.
episode_title: How Cryosite is turning frozen assets into hot growth
